questions.q: Adolescence is a critical period for bone density accretion. Which two nutrients are most critical to maximize peak bone mass during this stage?
questions.explain: Calcium is the main mineral in bone, and Vitamin D is required for its absorption. Approximately 45% of skeletal mass is added during adolescence.

questions.q: A 16-year-old female cross-country runner presents with amenorrhea, stress fractures, and restricted dietary intake. These signs describe which condition?
questions.explain: The Female Athlete Triad consists of three interrelated conditions: Low Energy Availability (with or without disordered eating), Amenorrhea (menstrual dysfunction), and Osteoporosis (low bone density).

questions.q: During the adolescent growth spurt, iron needs increase significantly. Why are the iron requirements for adolescent females higher than for males?
options: Females have a higher rate of muscle mass accumulation
Females lose iron due to the onset of menstruation
Females absorb iron less efficiently than males
questions.explain: Menstruation causes regular blood loss, thereby increasing the daily requirement for iron to replace losses.
